Hi Jordan / team,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached is our redline to the Order Form + a short list of questions from Legal. High level items we want to confirm before we proceed:
- Can Redwood guarantee operator credentials will never be used to access protected production data outside of documented witness windows?
- If operator access is required for troubleshooting, we need an auditable mechanism (timeboxed, recorded, and third-party witnessed).
- Do you have an escrow-style mechanism for operator runbooks and proof-of-access in case of prolonged vendor insolvency?

We flagged R1-R6 in the PDF. Please confirm what evidence you can provide (runbook excerpts, snapshot attestations, witness playbook).

Best,
Evan
Apex Health — Sr. Contracts Manager

Thanks Evan — appreciate the clear asks. Quick responses inline below, and an ask for a 30-min sync with Legal to go over the evidence package.

- Operator credential usage: We do not use operator credentials for routine access to customer data. Operator accounts are scoped to a maintenance role and require approval.
- Witnessing: We can provide recorded remote witness sessions and/or a short video capture of the exact steps taken during an operator intervention.
- Escrow-style runbook: We can provide a sealed runbook snapshot and a notarized attestation upon request. We also support a third-party escrow (we've worked with Kroll before).

Attachments: I attached a short runbook excerpt and our proposed witness checklist (Provisioning_Runbook_v1.docx).

Can your team do Thu 20 Nov 11am PT for a quick legal sync?

Lauren — For regulated apps handling PHI, Apex requires either (1) a standing 3rd-party witness for any operator access OR (2) an escrowed evidence path that includes sealed snapshots + documented witness runbook and a guaranteed window for independent verification in an insolvency event.

Kroll is preferred but not mandatory. Primary requirements are independence and ability to produce forensics with chain-of-custody.

We can discuss tradeoffs on the call.

— Evan

On Fri, 21 Nov 2025 at 08:45 AM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai> wrote:

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy - license carveouts and operator credentials

Evan — after internal review here are two pragmatic options we propose for the Order Form exhibit:

Option A (witness-first):
- Redwood agrees to recorded, signed witness sessions for any operator access that involves protected data.
- Sessions are timeboxed and include a signed log entry; recordings retained for 12 months (longer on request).
- Third-party witness can be arranged on a per-session basis at customer's cost.

Option B (escrow-evidence):
- Redwood will deposit a sealed, time-stamped snapshot of the runbook and a hashed snapshot of operator tooling with an independent escrow steward (e.g., Kroll).
- In insolvency or extended failure, escrow steward releases materials and provides verification access for a defined period.
- Redwood will commit to an annual witness drill to validate helpline procedures.

Which would Apex prefer as a baseline? We are open to combining elements (e.g., recorded sessions + escrowed runbook).

Thanks,
David
Head of Deployments, Redwood Inference

David — Option B is closer to what we need. A few clarifications:
- Escrow release criteria need to be explicit (insolvency, breach, failure-to-perform for X days).
- Access window on release should be at least 90 days and include read-only forensic access.
- Please include a sample escrow attestation statement that Kroll (or equivalent) would produce.

We can run redlines against your proposed exhibit if you provide a short draft.

Evan
